before.zh: 撤回之前，容闳替部分留美学生申请进入美国的军事院校，收到的答复是“没有为中国学生准备的名额”。对一个把孩子送去学工程、学海军的计划来说，这扇门开得很窄。
before.en: Before the recall, Yung Wing applied on behalf of some of the students for admission to American military academies. The answer he got was: "There is no room provided for Chinese students." For a program that sent children abroad to study engineering and naval science, that door opened only a crack.

before.zh: 1881年，约一百名学生被召回中国。耶鲁校长波特等人在致总理衙门的抗议信里说，这些年轻人“恰在他们就要收获此前学业最重要成果之时被带走”。从字面看，这是一次在投入即将兑现时的中止。
before.en: In 1881, about a hundred students were recalled to China. In their protest to the Zongli Yamen, Yale president Porter and others wrote that the young men had been taken away "just at the time when they were about to reap the most important advantages from their previous studies, and to gather in the rich harvest which their painful and laborious industry had been preparing for them to reap." Taken literally, this was a stop imposed at the moment the investment was about to pay off.

after.zh: 1870年代末，容闳为几名学业已经足够好的中国留学生，向美国国务院申请进入西点军校和安纳波利斯海军学院。答复只有一句：“没有为中国学生准备的位置。”容闳后来写道，他把这次碰壁报告给李鸿章，李的回信让他立刻明白，这个计划的命运已经注定。
after.en: In the late 1870s Yung Wing applied to the State Department for some of the Chinese students, by now far enough along in their studies, to enter the Military Academy at West Point and the Naval Academy at Annapolis. The answer was one line: "There is no room provided for Chinese students." When he reported the rebuff to Li Hongzhang, Yung later wrote, the reply "at once convinced me that the fate of the Mission was sealed".

after.zh: 1881年，大约一百名学生被召回国。耶鲁校长波特等人联名致信总理衙门，说这些年轻人恰在“就要从此前的学业中收获最重要成果”的时候被带走。
after.en: In 1881 about a hundred students were called home. President Porter of Yale and others wrote to the Zongli Yamen, China's foreign office, that the young men had been taken away "just at the time when they were about to reap the most important advantages from their previous studies".

reason: Academy application now evidenced (extended C-E7); 'room' kept literal; Porter's title and the addressee now evidenced (C-E15); removed unsupported '学工程、学海军' purpose.

before.zh: 同治十一年正月（1872年），两江总督曾国藩、直隶总督李鸿章奏请挑选幼童赴美国肄业，陈兰彬与容闳“蘭斌與閑同派管理學生，常川駐美”，也就是两人同管学生、长驻美国。按容闳后来的记述，总数一百二十人，分四批、每批三十人，每年一批；年龄不小于十二岁、不大于十五岁。家长或监护人须签字，声明愿意让儿子或受监护人出洋受教育十五年，不得反悔。1872年夏末，首批三十人抵达美国。
before.en: In the first month of the eleventh year of Tongzhi (1872), the Governor-General of Liangjiang, Zeng Guofan, and the Governor-General of Zhili, Li Hongzhang, memorialized the throne to select young boys for study in the United States. Chen Lanbin and Yung Wing were, in the words of the Qing history text, "jointly appointed to manage the students and to reside permanently in America" — that is, the two of them ran the program together and were posted to America on a long-term basis. By Yung Wing's later account, the total number was 120, sent in four installments of thirty, one installment a year; the boys were to be no younger than twelve and no older than fifteen. Parents or guardians had to sign a paper declaring that they were perfectly willing to let their sons or wards go abroad for fifteen years of education, with no turning back. In late summer 1872 the first group of thirty arrived in the United States.

after.zh: 这个计划始于同治十一年正月（1872年）：两江总督曾国藩、直隶总督李鸿章奏请挑选幼童赴美肄业，由陈兰彬和容闳管理学生、常驻美国。按容闳的记述，计划共送一百二十人，分四批、每年三十人；年龄十二到十五岁；家长要签字，同意孩子出洋读书十五年。1872年夏末，第一批三十人准备横渡太平洋。
after.en: The programme began in the first month of the eleventh year of Tongzhi (1872), when Zeng Guofan, Viceroy of Liangjiang, and Li Hongzhang, Viceroy of Zhili, asked the throne to send selected boys to study in America, with Chen Lanbin and Yung Wing to manage them and live in the United States. By Yung Wing's account the plan was for 120 boys in four groups of 30, one group a year, aged twelve to fifteen; parents had to sign a paper agreeing to fifteen years of study abroad. In late summer 1872 the first thirty were ready to cross the Pacific.

reason: Kept; quoted 清史纪事本末 spelling disclosed instead of mixing the raw quote into prose.

before.zh: 学生住进美国人家中、进学校读书，随之改穿服装，参加家庭礼拜、主日学与教堂礼拜，做户外运动、玩球类。容闳记他与陈兰彬在这些事上争执，学生费用也在争执之列。一种解释是：这些日常之所以要紧，是因为在两套标准下它们指向相反的结论——在一边是适应与融入，在另一边是“忘本”的证据。
before.en: The students moved into American homes and attended American schools. Soon they changed their dress, took part in family worship, Sunday school and church services, and played outdoor sports and ball games. Yung Wing records quarrels with Chen Lanbin over these matters, and the students' expenses were disputed as well. One way to read this: these daily details mattered because under two sets of standards they pointed to opposite conclusions — on one side, adaptation and fitting in; on the other, evidence of "forgetting one's roots."

before.zh: 新任监督 Woo Tsze Tung 到任后向北京寄送报告。以下内容均出自容闳的转述：学生玩多学少，被容闳纵容，模仿美国学生搞体育，结成宗教与政治性质的秘密社团，不听新监督的劝告；多数人上教堂、进主日学、成了基督徒；这个教育事业越早解散、学生越早撤回，对中国越好。容闳还说此人“被朋友们视为怪人”——这是容闳的敌意描述，不能当作评价。
before.en: After the new commissioner, Woo Tsze Tung, took office, he began sending reports to Peking. Everything that follows comes from Yung Wing's retelling: the students played more than they studied; they were indulged and petted by Commissioner Yung; they imitated American students in athletics; they formed secret societies, religious and political; they would not listen to the new commissioner's advice; most of them went to church, attended Sunday schools and had become Christians; and the sooner this educational enterprise was broken up and the students recalled, the better for China. Yung Wing also wrote that the man "was regarded by all his friends as a crank" — but that is Yung Wing's hostile characterization and cannot be taken as an assessment.

before.zh: 随后是一份御史的奏请。按容闳的说法，这位御史利用美国的强烈排华情绪，奏请解散学局、撤回全体学生；排华氛围这一背景同样出自容闳之笔。朝廷先问李鸿章，李鸿章同意撤回；再问被认为最有经验的陈兰彬，他判断学生在美已经够久、该回去了；Woo Tsze Tung 主张立即撤回、回国后严加看管。容闳被排除在咨询之外。约一百名学生于1881年回国。
before.en: Then a censor submitted a memorial. In Yung Wing's telling, this censor took advantage of the strong anti-Chinese prejudices in America to memorialize the government to break up the Mission and recall all the students; the anti-Chinese atmosphere as background likewise comes from Yung Wing's pen. The court first asked Li Hongzhang, who agreed to the recall. Next it asked Chen Lanbin, thought to know best from his own experience; he decided the students had been in America long enough and should return. Woo Tsze Tung called for them to be recalled without delay and closely watched after their return. Yung Wing was ruled out of the consultation altogether. About a hundred students returned to China in 1881.

before.zh: 抗议信里还有一句为自己撇清的话：如果学生忘了中文，“我们从未承担教授他们母语的责任”。这封信的文本，我们是通过容闳的书看到的。
before.en: The protest letter also contains one line that clears its authors of blame: if the students had neglected or forgotten their native language, "we never assumed the duty of instructing them in it, and cannot be held responsible for this neglect." We see the text of this letter only as reprinted in Yung Wing's book.

before.zh: 记住一个具体的人：詹天佑。据1917年《游美同学录》记载，他初学于上海出洋局，同治十一年以官费赴美，光绪四年入耶路大学习土木工程，光绪七年得学士学位，被选入某名誉学会，以数学成绩得奖，同年回国，先肄业于福州船政局水师学堂。而他历任京张铁路等路的总工程师、副工程师等职，要从光绪十四年才开始。从学到用，中间隔了七年。
before.en: Keep one specific person in mind: Zhan Tianyou. According to the 1917 Record of Students Returned from America, he first studied at the Shanghai Educational Mission; in the eleventh year of Tongzhi he went to America on a government scholarship; in the fourth year of Guangxu he entered Yale University to study civil engineering; in the seventh year of Guangxu he received a bachelor's degree, was elected to an honorary society and won a mathematics prize; the same year he returned home and first studied at the naval academy of the Fuzhou Shipyard. His posts as chief engineer, assistant engineer and similar titles on the Beijing–Zhangjiakou Railway and other lines did not begin until the fourteenth year of Guangxu. From study to practice there was a gap of seven years.

after.zh: 到了新英格兰，分歧先出现在日常小事上。容闳列出他与陈兰彬反复争执的事项：学生的学费和零用、假期开销、改换服装、参加家庭礼拜、去主日学和教堂、户外运动和球类。容闳说，他夹在中间当“缓冲”，为学生的合理要求辩护。
after.en: In New England the disagreements began with everyday things. Yung Wing lists the matters he and Chen Lanbin fought over: the students' school and personal expenses, vacation expenses, their change of dress, attending family worship, Sunday school and church, and outdoor exercise and athletic games. Yung says he had to stand as "a kind of buffer" between Chen and the students.

after.zh: 1876年秋，Woo Tsze Tung 接任监督。以下都出自容闳的转述：此人一上任就处处挑错，又不当面提出，而是不断向北京写信，说学生管理失当、被容闳纵容，模仿美国学生搞体育，玩多学少，结成宗教和政治性质的秘密团体，不听新监督的话，许多人上教堂、成了基督徒，再这样下去会忘了自己的国家；越早解散、全部撤回，对中国越好。容闳还说此人一向被朋友们“视为怪人”——这是当事一方的敌意描述。
after.en: In the autumn of 1876 Woo Tsze Tung became commissioner. What follows is Yung Wing's account. Woo found fault with everything and, instead of raising it with Yung, sent a stream of letters to Peking: the students had been mismanaged and petted by Yung; they imitated American students in athletics and played more than they studied; they formed secret societies, religious and political; they ignored the new commissioner; most went to church and had become Christians; left alone they would lose their love of their country; and the "sooner this educational enterprise was broken up and all the students recalled, the better it would be for China". Yung adds that Woo "was regarded by all his friends as a crank", a hostile description from an interested party.

after.zh: 军校申请碰壁后，Woo 再次发力，据容闳说，这一次有陈兰彬暗中配合。一位御史借美国的排华情绪上奏，请求解散留学事务、撤回全部学生。朝廷先征询李鸿章，他同意撤回；再问陈兰彬，他认为学生在美已经够久；Woo 主张立即撤回、回国后严加看管。容闳则被完全排除在征询之外。1881年，约一百名学生全部回国。
after.en: After the academies' refusal, Woo renewed his efforts, this time, Yung says, with Chen Lanbin's secret co-operation. A censor, taking advantage of anti-Chinese feeling in America, asked the throne to break up the Mission and recall all the students. The court asked Li Hongzhang first, and he agreed. Chen Lanbin judged that the students had been in America long enough. Woo said they should be recalled without delay and closely watched after their return. Yung was "ruled out of the consultation altogether". In 1881 about a hundred students returned to China.

after.zh: 美国的教师和监护人们联名抗议。除了“正要收获”那一句，他们还写道：“我们尚未完成交给我们的工作”，成果却在完成之前就被否定；至于学生若忘了中文，“我们从未承担教他们母语的责任”。这封信，我们今天是通过容闳书中的转载读到的。
after.en: The students' American teachers and guardians protested. Besides the line about the harvest, they wrote: "We have not finished the work which we were expected to perform." Why should the results "be judged unfavorably before it could possibly be finished"? As for any neglect of Chinese, "we never assumed the duty of instructing them in it". We can read the letter today only because Yung Wing reprinted it in his book.

after.zh: 记住一个具体的人：詹天佑。据1917年的《游美同学录》，他同治十一年（1872）以官费赴美，光绪四年（1878）进耶鲁大学（原书作“耶路大學”）学土木工程，光绪七年（1881）得学士学位，以数学成绩获奖，同年回国。回国后，他先被安排进福州船政局的水师学堂；从光绪十四年（1888）起，才历任京张铁路等多条铁路的工程师、总工程师。
after.en: Keep one person in mind: Zhan Tianyou. According to the 1917 alumni record, he went to America on a government scholarship in 1872, entered Yale in 1878 to study civil engineering, took his bachelor's degree in 1881 with a prize for mathematics, and returned to China that same year. He was first placed at the naval school of the Fuzhou shipyard. Only from 1888 did he hold engineering posts on the railways, eventually as chief engineer on the Peking–Kalgan line and others.

reason: Removed unsupported '住进美国人家中'; expenses now evidenced (extended C-E4); dated Woo's start (extended C-E5); Chen Lanbin's secret co-operation (extended C-E8); added the teachers' 'not finished' argument (C-E17); kept Zhan Tianyou's dated record.

before.zh: 一个可以确认的结构性原因是：评估权和执行权分了家，中期汇报又几乎只走一条渠道。学生的学业进度并非无迹可循，波特等人的信本身就是一份来自校方的记录；但正式报到北京的意见，来自监督一方的报告（C-E5），而最了解学生日常的容闳被排除在咨询之外（C-E9）。结果是，用来判断的指标变成了“是否入教、是否忘本、是否玩多学少”，而不是课程、考试与学位进度。
before.en: One structural reason we can confirm is that the power to evaluate and the power to act were separated, and mid-course reporting went through almost a single channel. The students' academic progress was not untraceable — the letter from Porter and others is itself a record from the university side — but the formal opinion reported to Peking came from the commissioner's reports (C-E5), while Yung Wing, who knew the students' daily lives best, was ruled out of the consultation (C-E9). So the indicators used for judgment became whether they had converted to Christianity, whether they had forgotten their roots, and whether they played more than they studied, instead of courses, exams and progress toward degrees.

before.zh: 另一点是时间点。抗议信里的“收获”一词，指向的是投入—回报曲线的最后一段（C-E10）：派出去九年，最快的那批人刚好拿到学位。一种解释是，当争议上升到“这些孩子还是不是我们的人”，可核对的专业成绩就不再是主要议题；但这是作者的推断，现有材料无法证明决策者当时如何权衡，也无法证明如果詹天佑们早两年毕业，结论会不会不同——这个反事实同样由作者提出。
before.en: A second point is the timing. The word "harvest" in the protest letter points to the final stretch of the investment-return curve (C-E10): nine years after the boys were sent out, the fastest group had just earned their degrees. One possible reading is that once the dispute turned into "are these children still our people," checkable academic results were no longer the main issue. But this is the author's inference. The available material cannot show how the decision-makers weighed things at the time, nor whether the conclusion would have differed if Zhan Tianyou and his classmates had graduated two years earlier — this counterfactual too comes from the author.

after.zh: 这不是一个人的决定。容闳记下的是一条链：监督的报告、军校的拒绝、御史的奏折、朝廷对三位官员的征询。一种解释是（作者推断）：决定所依据的，主要是学生“变成了什么样的人”，而不是他们学会了什么；最能说明学业的人——容闳和美国的教师们——都不在征询之列。不过清廷撤回的奏折原文本篇没有取得，决策者当时究竟怎样权衡，现有材料证明不了。
after.en: This was not one person's decision. What Yung records is a chain: the commissioner's reports, the academies' refusal, the censor's memorial, the court consulting three officials. One interpretation, the author's, is that the decision turned mainly on what kind of people the students were becoming, not on what they had learned, and that those best placed to speak to their studies, Yung Wing and the American teachers, were not among those consulted. But this article has not obtained the Qing memorials on the recall, and the material we have cannot show how the decision-makers actually weighed the question.

after.zh: 另一点是时间。按原计划，学生要在美国读十五年；召回时，最早一批去了大约九年。詹天佑恰好赶上毕业，而他学到的本事，又过了七年才用上。长期投入最容易在“快见效、还没见效”的时候被叫停——这是作者的观察，不是史料的结论。
after.en: The other point is timing. The plan called for fifteen years; when the recall came, the first group had been in America about nine. Zhan Tianyou happened to graduate just in time, and even then his training waited seven more years to be put to use. Long-term investments are most easily stopped when they are close to paying off but have not yet done so; that is the author's observation, not a finding of the sources.

reason: Draft stated a structural model as established fact and said reports came through 'one channel' although three officials were consulted; rewritten as marked interpretation; '最快的那批人刚好拿到学位' removed (degree documented only for Zhan).

before.zh: 现代虚构场景：一个三年期的跨部门轮岗试点进行到第二年半，业务部门抱怨轮岗生“不像我们的人”，项目组却说他们的产出刚要上来。可以借的做法是：开项时就把中期评估看哪些指标写清楚（产出、考核、留任意愿各占多少），并规定评估会上执行方、用人方、学员三方都要到场，别让汇报只从一条线路进来。
before.en: Modern fictional scenario: a three-year cross-department rotation pilot is two and a half years in. Business units complain that the participants "are not like our people," while the project team says their output is just about to take off. One method worth borrowing: at the launch, spell out which indicators the mid-term review will use and how they are weighted (output, assessments, retention intent), and require the implementing side, the hiring side and the participants all to attend the review, so that reports do not arrive along a single line.

before.zh: 现代虚构场景：一支团队外派培训，学员业余扎进行业社群，有人担心“心散了”。可以借的做法是把“行为变化”和“能力损失”分开：前者要看是否影响事先约定的产出，后者用可核对的证书、项目、考试成绩说话；写评估结论时，注明哪些是记录、哪些是印象。
before.en: Modern fictional scenario: a team is sent out for training, the participants spend their spare time in industry communities, and some people worry their "minds have scattered." One method worth borrowing is to separate "behavior change" from "capability loss": the first is judged by whether it affects the outputs agreed in advance; the second is argued with checkable certificates, projects and exam results. When writing up review conclusions, state which parts are records and which are impressions.

after.zh: 一个新组建的数据团队，产出要九个月后才看得见，公司却按惯例在第三个月做评估。评估人看到的是“还没做出东西”，外加几件不合群的小事。可以先做一件事：项目开始时就写下“什么时候、用什么指标算见效”，并请最了解工作内容的人参加评估，别让中途的印象替代约定的指标。
after.en: A newly formed data team will not show results for nine months, but the company reviews it at three, as usual. The reviewers see "nothing delivered yet" plus a few awkward habits. One thing to do first: at the start, write down when the work should count as paying off and by which measures, and have the people who best understand the work sit in on the review, so that mid-course impressions do not replace the agreed measures.

after.zh: 现代虚构场景：一支团队外派培训，学员业余扎进行业社群，有人担心“心散了”。可以借的做法是把“行为变化”和“能力损失”分开：前者要看是否影响事先约定的产出，后者用可核对的证书、项目、考试成绩说话；写评估结论时，注明哪些是记录、哪些是印象。
after.en: Modern fictional scenario: a team is sent out for training, the participants spend their spare time in industry communities, and some people worry their "minds have scattered." One method worth borrowing is to separate "behavior change" from "capability loss": the first is judged by whether it affects the outputs agreed in advance; the second is argued with checkable certificates, projects and exam results. When writing up review conclusions, state which parts are records and which are impressions.

reason: First scene duplicated the reflection's 2.5-year rotation scenario; replaced with an evaluation-timing scene. Second scene kept.

before.zh: 本篇关于撤回经过与理由的叙述，主要来自容闳1909年的回忆录，他是当事一方，对陈兰彬与 Woo Tsze Tung 带有强烈敌意；清廷撤回奏折的原文本篇未取得。“Woo Tsze Tung 一般认为即吴子登”这条对应关系，本证据包没有直接证明，只能列为待核实背景。美国排华氛围同样是容闳的描述，波特抗议信的文本也只见于容闳书中的转载。所以“为什么撤回”这个问题，现有材料给出的是一面之词加一封抗议信，不足以定论，更不宜当作组织决策的范本。
before.en: The account of the recall and its reasons here comes mainly from Yung Wing's 1909 memoir. He was one of the parties involved and was strongly hostile to Chen Lanbin and Woo Tsze Tung. The original text of the Qing court's recall memorial was not obtained for this piece. The identification "Woo Tsze Tung is generally taken to be Wu Zideng" is not directly supported by this evidence packet and can only be listed as background to be verified. The anti-Chinese atmosphere in America is likewise Yung Wing's description, and the text of Porter's protest is known only as reprinted in Yung Wing's book. So on the question "why were they recalled," the available material gives one side's account plus one protest letter — not enough for a settled verdict, and certainly not something to treat as a model of organizational decision-making.
